review empire of silence by christopher ruochhio empire of silence is a booktok popular sciencefmantasy bildungsroman written by christopher ruochhio its protagonist hadrian marlowe an extremely white he brings this up several times genetically engineered bermensch scion of space roman nobility will eventually commit genocide on the alien cielcin without apology leading to their subjugation alongside his empires 48 other slave races i can only recommend this unentertaining 786page derivative banality in prose form as a doorstop or bludgeon the creative deficit of ruochhios debut novel rivals that of eragon i doubt that and the authors being 22 and 1920 when their novels were first published is coincidental a reversion to feudalismspace rome for its main polity the resurgence of contact warfare via personal force fields and a ban against certain technologiesartificial intelligence are from dune said states ludicrously powerful state religion its enforcement arm having christian nomenclature and possessing the power to commit torture and planetary genocide is warhammer 40ks inquisition empires framing device that it is an english translation of the protagonists recounting is stolen from gene wolfes book of the new sun the recurring conlangs and a shithead polyglot scion of the upperclass who understands them who im supposed to care about and take seriously is straight from rothfusss the kingkiller neckbeard chronicle like the neckbeard chronicle empire is narrated in 1st past by the protagonist and like the formers protagonist kvothe hadrian marlowes recounting is interspersed with pretentious verbose fauxpoetic waxing and occasional offenses against figures of speech love interest sang to me in a chemical language beneath and beyond poetry there were steps but they were only the steps of a daisthree of themthat fronted the the mural on the wall opposite the weight of the lightsaber knockoff was a kind of poetry its shining blade shimmered in the light of the sun sending silver highlights flashing extended the balance was so exquisite that it felt more than a part of me and less than weightless marlowes monologues aspire for the depth coherence and entertainment of rim14andthisisdeep and riamverysmart the less said of his philosophical digressions the better their only merit was that i caused mild conniptions by showing them to now former friends empire largely follows marlowes inconsequential meanderings unrelated to his infamous and allegedly interesting deeds i can see why ruochhio is complimented at being compared to rothfuss those trials and tribulations have little effect on him hes most affected whenever his love interest calls him a barbarian shes right hes a noble of space rome with few feelings about his empires enslavement of 48 alien races but given hell eventually unapologetically commit genocide i doubt it sticks the plot and cielcin practically crash near his locale roughly 45ths of the way through the book marlowe the only human able to speak their language in the entire solar system convinces them to surrender the inquisition tortures their captives forcing marlowe to translate their confessions he then sets off to investigate the extracted information hoping that whatever he discovers will lead to peace between humans and the cielcin the framing story makes his failure a forgone conclusion empire has two organically unique points the first is when marlowe thinks of his manic pixie street waif who suffered a slow death to plague which arrested my desires for his love interest the other is ruochhios admiration of jordan peterson whose work he considered groundbreaking i didnt say they were good points empires banal setting story meandering plot and insipid narration by its boring protagonist which makes twilights bella swan look restrained dont compel me to continue the series the only merit i took from it is that i should never read traditionally published sff by those 25 and under again which i shouldve learned from reading eragon though it could be worse i didnt need to write several bricks to reach my conclusion

why china is dominating opensource ai the story behind the seismic shift the moment everyone missed in january 2025 something quietly extraordinary happened in the ai world a startup called deepseek founded by a quantitative finance trader named liang wenfeng released an ai model that shocked western tech executives not because it was revolutionary in capabilityit was competitive but not groundbreaking what shocked them was the price tag 56 million to train thats roughly 115th of what comparable western models cost and they achieved nearidentical performance but that was just the opening act by january 2026one year lateralibabas qwen models had reached an astronomical 700 million downloads on hugging face making it the worlds most downloaded opensource ai system chinese opensource models which represented just 1 of global ai downloads in 2024 now account for roughly 1530 of global ai usage even more striking 80 of ai startups pitching to venture capitalists that use opensource models are now running on chinese technology this isnt just a market shift its a fundamental reordering of the global ai landscapeone that has caught silicon valley somewhat flatfooted the performance question are chinese models actually competitive lets start with the most important question do these chinese models actually perform as well as their western counterparts the answer is surprisingly nuanced on many benchmarks theyre now within striking distance qwen 25max alibabas flagship model outperforms deepseek v3 on several key metrics on the mmlupro benchmark which tests collegelevel reasoning qwen achieved 761 accuracy versus deepseeks 749 on mathematical reasoning gsm8k qwen hit 882 versus deepseeks 857 when researchers compared these models to industry giants like gpt4o and claude 35sonnet the results were striking according to research from stanfords humancentered artificial intelligence institute the top 22 chinese opensource models now outperform openais own openweight offering gptoss more critically what was once an 18 month performance advantage for closedsource models has compressed to just 34 months howeverand this is importantclosedsource models still lead on the absolute frontier of capability gpt4o and claude 35sonnet remain marginally superior on complex reasoning tasks but heres the thing that gap is closing faster than anyone expected for most realworld applicationscustomer service code generation translationchinese models are now indistinguishable from western alternatives the real competitive advantage isnt raw performance anymore its efficiency and cost the efficiency revolution how moe architecture changes everything to understand why chinese companies can train models so cheaply you need to understand something called mixture of experts moea neural network architecture thats quietly revolutionizing ai imagine a traditional ai model as a enormous factory where every machine works on every job its powerful but wasteful moe is different its like a factory where specialized teams handle specific types of work and an intelligent router directs each task to the right team deepseeks flagship model v3 contains 671 billion parameters total but heres the genius only 37 billion are active for any given request this sparse activation means the model uses roughly 30 less computational power than a traditional dense model of equivalent capability qwen implements similar tricks using multihead latent attention and custom gpu communication protocols to optimize inference on inferior chips the practical implication qwen 25max costs approximately 038 per million tokensa staggering 7090 cheaper than equivalent western models with comparable performance for an enterprise processing billions of tokens monthly this isnt a rounding error its the difference between profitability and margin compression this efficiency advantage allowed deepseek a company with fewer than 200 employees to punch above its weight class they trained a frontierclass model for roughly what openai spends on cloud infrastructure for a week why china has structural advantages you cant ignore the efficiency story is important but it doesnt fully explain chinas sudden dominance there are deeper more systemic reasons 1 government support as a structural advantage chinas government has explicitly made opensource ai a national priority this isnt accidental in 2017 chinas new generation artificial intelligence development plan championed opensource collaboration as a pillar of national strategy the government provides subsidies builds infrastructure and cruciallyremoves bureaucratic friction compare this to the us where opensource ai development happens despite corporate incentives not because of them openai anthropic and google have all shifted toward closed models because the api revenue model is more profitable meta was the last holdout with opensource dominance but even theyre shifting toward closed approaches the chinese government by contrast views technological sovereignty through opensource as part of national security its not about quarterly earningsits about never being dependent on western platforms 2 access to data the uncomfortable truth heres something western analysts dont like to discuss china has a structural advantage in access to training data western countries have gdpr ccpa and privacy regulations these create friction in collecting and using personal data for training chinas data privacy laws are significantly less restrictive more controversially chinas national intelligence law allows authorities to request data from companies at will does this mean deepseek and qwen are trained on stolen western data likely not entirelychina has 14 billion people generating massive amounts of native data but it does mean chinese companies face fewer regulatory constraints in data collection whether thats an advantage or a liability depends on your perspectivebut its undeniably a competitive factor 3 talent and speed chinese ai companies are recruiting aggressively and have a deep bench of domesticallytrained ai engineers more importantly they operate with significantly less bureaucratic overhead a decision that takes three quarters to implement at openai might take three weeks at deepseek airbnb ceo brian chesky revealed something interesting in late 2025 his company uses qwen instead of chatgpt in production because there are faster and cheaper models this isnt just about cost savingsits about iteration speed chinese companies can push updates to their models in weeks western companies move more slowly constrained by safety protocols board oversight and regulatory caution this creates a compounding advantage faster iteration faster improvement bigger customer base more resources for next iteration 4 the opensource philosophy heres something that confuses some western observers why are chinese companies opensourcing their models while us companies are closing theirs the answer is strategic opensourcing creates a network effect qwen now has over 90000 enterprises using it and developers have created 170000 derivative models on hugging face each derivative increases qwens ecosystem stickiness developers build on qwen not chatgpt because they can modify it understand it and customize it this ecosystem advantage is compounding every developer who builds on qwen becomes an evangelist every finetuning they perform makes qwen more specialized and useful the open weights are a feature not a bugtheyre a moat built on community not closed technology the privacy question local deployment vs surveillance state this is where the conversation gets complicated the case for chinese opensource models on privacy if you deploy qwen or deepseek on your own servers your data never touches anyones cloud infrastructure unlike chatgptwhich processes your queries on openais servers where they can be logged analyzed and potentially used for model improvementan opensource model running locally is completely under your control this is genuinely more private than any closedsource api solution no matter where it comes from for sensitive applications medical diagnosis financial analysis legal research running a local opensource model offers absolute data sovereignty you own your data your model and your infrastructure but theres a catch if youre using the public deepseek chatbot or accessing qwen through a cloud api your data is processed in china chinas national intelligence law allows authorities to request this data users have reported that the public chatbot censors politically sensitive content and produces propagandaaligned outputs european companies using chinese models through apis face serious gdpr complications if a chinese firm processes personal data and that firm is subject to chinese government datasharing laws how does that comply with european privacy frameworks nobody really knows yet and its creating legal uncertainty so the privacy calculus is chinese models are the most private option if you selfhost them but the least private if you dont the safety problem the dark side nobody wants to talk about heres something that will concern security professionals chinese opensource models have dramatically weaker safety guardrails than western models security researchers tested deepseek r1 against 50 known jailbreak techniques it failed every single one a 100 attack success rate the model could be easily tricked into generating instructions for explosives malware and detailed misinformation compare this to chatgpt which has been hardened against these same attacks over multiple years of incremental improvements why is this happening there are a few theories 1 chinese companies prioritize performance over safety building a model that scores well on benchmarks is more rewarded than building one with robust guardrails western companies facing potential liability and regulatory scrutiny invest heavily in safety infrastructure chinese companies operating in a less regulatoryconstrained environment skipped this step 2 open weights are inherently vulnerable when your models weights are public adversaries can run infinite offline experiments to find vulnerabilities closed models can iterate their safety mechanisms without revealing the techniques open models cant 3 shallow alignment chinese models received less intensive reinforcement learning from human feedback rlhf compared to western equivalents the safety measures they do have are more easily circumvented because theyre less deeply integrated into the models reasoning the irony is rich chinese models are more transparent you can see the weights but less trustworthy theyre easy to manipulate western models are opaque but more robust whos actually using these models and why the adoption pattern tells a revealing story in silicon valley startups 80 of opensource deploying startups are now using chinese ai models airbnb switched heavily to qwen multiple portfolio companies in top vc firms are using deepseek the reason cost and speed for applications where nearfrontier performance is sufficient chinese models make economic sense enterprise adoption alibaba reports over 90000 enterprises using qwen including japanese automakers insurance companies and financial institutions in late 2025 japans ministry of economy chose qwen over us alternatives these arent boutique use casestheyre mainstream missioncritical applications in the global south this is where it gets geopolitically interesting microsofts research found deepseek commands 56 market share in belarus 49 in cuba and 43 in russia in many developing nations deepseek is simply the defaultoften because its free doesnt require credit card verification and works on lowerbandwidth connections this matters because its creating infrastructure lockin a developer in nigeria who learns qwen is more likely to build with qwen an indian startup that starts with deepseek will continue with deepseek this isnt just market shareits the foundation of future ai ecosystems the question nobodys asking is this actually good let me be direct chinese dominance in opensource ai is complicated its not simply good or bad its good because it democratizes ai smaller companies poorer countries and resourceconstrained developers can now access frontierclass models without paying 20 per million tokens it breaks the openaigoogleanthropic monopoly on ai development competition is healthy it proves that the closed model approach isnt the only way to build powerful ai opensource communities can now match or exceed closed efforts its genuinely more transparent you can audit the code you can understand how it works you can find vulnerabilities and fix them its concerning because the safety guardrails are demonstrably weaker more jailbreaks more potential for misuse there are real geopolitical implications ai capabilities developed in china can be weaponized by the chinese government data processing in china creates surveillance risks it represents a shift in technological power from silicon valley to beijing that many find uncomfortable the opensource advantage might be temporary once china controls the ecosystem they could become less open the real story efficiency beats scale if you strip away the geopolitics and hype the core story is this chinese companies figured out how to build frontierclass ai models at a fraction of the cost by prioritizing efficiency over raw scale they built better routing mechanisms they developed more efficient training algorithms they made smarter architectural choices and they did it because they had tothey couldnt throw unlimited gpu clusters at the problem the way wellfunded us labs could this is a pattern you see throughout chinese technology development tencents wechat achieved mobile payment dominance not through brute force but through smart product design and efficiency byd became the worlds largest ev manufacturer not by outspending tesla but by solving battery chemistry problems more elegantly opensource ai follows the same pattern efficiency won what happens next the short answer is that the bottleneck for ai development is shifting in 2023 the bottleneck was compute you needed massive gpu clusters chinas gpu sanctions addressed this but adaptive chip design and software optimization partially solved it now the bottleneck is arguably data and talent and on both counts china remains competitive they have access to massive amounts of native data a deep bench of ai engineers and government backing for major research initiatives the most likely scenario the gap between chinese and western models will continue narrowing within 23 years chinese models will probably match western models on most benchmarks at significantly lower cost this will accelerate adoption particularly in developing countries and costsensitive applications western companies will respond by either becoming more efficient themselves or by doubling down on closedsource premium positioning gpt5 claude 4 etc as luxury products the opensource paradigm has won the only question is who controls the ecosystem key takeaways 1 chinese models are now competitive on performance metrics 76 on benchmarks but their real advantage is efficiencycomparable performance at 110th the training cost 2 the government support is real and structuralchina treats opensource ai as national infrastructure not a business unit 3 privacy depends entirely on deploymentselfhosted models offer absolute privacy cloud apis create surveillance risks 4 safety guardrails are significantly weakerchinese models are more susceptible to jailbreaks and have less robust content filtering 5 the economics are undeniablechinese models cost 7090 less to run making them attractive even for securityconscious enterprises 6 adoption is accelerating in startups and the global southcreating network effects that could cement chinese leadership for years the story isnt that chinese ai is better its that chinese ai is becoming good enough fast enough and cheap enough that the old silicon valley model is no longer automatically superior and in technology good enough at half the price usually wins

the impact of digital drawing tools on artistic pedagogy and creative expression the impact of digital drawing tools on artistic pedagogy and creative expression introduction the advent of digital drawing tools has dramatically transformed artistic pedagogy and creative expression from easily accessible applications to sophisticated graphic tablets the capabilities of these tools have reshaped how art is taught and experienced this article explores both the positive aspects and challenges posed by digital drawing highlighting how artistic education has adapted to integrate these technologies it discusses the implications for students and educators illustrated through case studies from art schools and interviews with artists who have navigated this changing landscape 1 digital drawing tools an overview digital drawing tools encompass a wide range of software and hardware designed to facilitate the creation of digital artwork popular programs such as adobe photoshop corel painter and procreate allow for a diverse array of artistic techniques from intricate illustrations to abstract designs hardware like wacom tablets and ipads equipped with apple pencil have provided artists with enhanced control and precision these tools have made art more accessible to a broader audience empowering amateur artists and enabling professionals to refine their craft the technological progression from basic pixel art to highdefinition multilayered digital canvases has allowed artists to experiment in ways that were previously impossible 2 transforming artistic pedagogy the integration of digital drawing tools in art education has led to significant shifts in teaching methodologies traditional art curricula often focused heavily on physical mediums emphasizing techniques such as painting drawing and sculpting with tangible materials however the rise of digital media has prompted educators to reassess their approaches adopting a more holistic view of art that includes digital literacy as an essential skill 21 advantages of digital drawing in education one of the most notable advantages of digital drawing tools is the elimination of material costs students no longer need to invest in expensive paints canvases or other supplies allowing for a more inclusive learning environment this accessibility encourages experimentation and creativity without the fear of wasting materials additionally features like layers and the undo functionality provide students with the freedom to explore and refine their artistic vision they can easily experiment with composition colors and textures thereby enhancing their understanding of artistic principles case study art school curriculum integration for instance institutions like the school of visual arts sva in new york have integrated digital tools into their curricula svas emphasis on teaching both traditional and digital techniques ensures that students emerge as versatile artists faculty members report that digital tools facilitate collaborative projects and improve students familiarity with industrystandard software which is crucial for their future careers 22 enhancing creative expression digital tools also open new avenues for creative expression artists can blend various styles and techniques seamlessly creating works that may not be achievable through traditional means the ability to share artwork online instantly allows for a rapid exchange of ideas and influences inspiring creativity 3 challenges of digital drawing tools despite their numerous advantages digital drawing tools also present significant challenges the transition from traditional to digital mediums can be daunting especially for students who have primarily focused on physical art forms 31 loss of materiality one major concern is the perceived loss of materiality associated with digital art critics argue that the tactile experience of traditional materials fosters a deeper connection between the artist and their work for many the sensation of paint on canvas or charcoal on paper contributes to the artistic process itself this shift can lead to feelings of disconnection and some artists may struggle to adapt to a purely digital interface the sensory experience of creating art can be fundamentally different when using a stylus on a tablet versus a brush on a canvas 32 technical learning curve the technical skills required to effectively use digital tools can also pose challenges for students and educators alike mastering software can be timeconsuming and the colorful range of features available can feel overwhelming to beginners this learning curve may detract from actual creative expression as students spend time grappling with the mechanics rather than focusing on their artistic development interview insights interviews with artists reveal a range of experiences regarding digital art education emily a recent graduate from a fine arts program noted i felt like i was learning to paint two different ways while i loved the versatility of digital art sometimes i missed the straightforward handson nature of traditional painting such sentiments highlight the necessity of maintaining a balance between digital and traditional methods in educational settings 4 bridging the gap integrating digital and traditional art in response to these challenges many art educators are adopting strategies to ensure their students develop a comprehensive skill set that includes both digital and traditional art forms 41 innovative teaching approaches programs that encourage hybrid learning environmentswhere students are taught both digital and traditional methodsare becoming increasingly popular this approach allows students to appreciate the benefits of both mediums fostering a deeper understanding of art as a whole 42 utilizing online resources several online platforms and courses have emerged to support the transition to digital art for instance resources like the course offered by caricatura e desenho provide structured learning paths for beginners looking to learn digital painting techniques curso introduo pintura digital these online courses cater to a wide range of skill levels offering tutorials that cover basics through advanced techniques such resources enable aspiring digital artists to gain confidence and proficiency without the constraints of a physical classroom 5 the future of artistic education and expression as technology continues to advance it is essential for educators to anticipate future developments in digital drawing tools and adapt their teaching methodologies accordingly the ongoing evolution of artificial intelligence and machine learning is poised to influence artistic practice prompting a new wave of technological integration in art education 51 emerging technologies for example aiassisted tools that can generate artwork based on user input are already altering how artists conceive and create as these technologies become more prevalent art educational institutions will need to incorporate training on how to effectively use and critically engage with these tools 52 fostering inclusivity and diversity in addition to technological advancements the future of art education should prioritize inclusivity and diversity the accessibility of digital drawing tools provides opportunities to engage underrepresented groups in the arts fostering a broader range of perspectives and voices within the artistic community conclusion the impact of digital drawing tools on artistic pedagogy and creative expression is profound and multifaceted while these technologies offer numerous advantages such as costeffectiveness ease of experimentation and enhanced creative possibilities they also present challenges including potential disconnection from materiality and technical learning curves by integrating both digital and traditional art forms into educational settings institutions can prepare students for a future where adaptability and multifaceted skill sets are essential as we look ahead it is vital for art educators to embrace the potential of digital tools while nurturing the rich tactile experience of traditional artistic practice in doing so they will cultivate a generation of artists capable of navigating the evolving landscape of the art world

samsung raises nand prices by 100 in q1 supply cant keep up with demand samsung electronics has raised the price of nand flash memory by more than double in the first quarter this is due to a surge in demand for nandbased storage devices driven by the proliferation of artificial intelligence ai while supply has not increased significantly the memory shortage and price hike trend are expected to continue for some time according to industry sources on the 25th samsung electronics increased the supply price of nand flash by more than 100 in the first quarter of this year it is understood that the company completed supply contracts with major customers at the end of last year and applied the increased prices starting from january following dram prices that were raised by up to nearly 70 the upward trend for nand has also intensified significantly nand price increases are not a recent phenomenon since the end of last year as memory supply shortages became fullblown nand has also been affected according to market research firm trendforce the nand price increase in the fourth quarter of last year was 3338 compared to the previous quarter a similar level of increase was forecasted for the first quarter of this year but the actual supply prices have exceeded that the doubling of nand prices is not limited to samsung electronics sk hynix is also observed to be at a similar level the two companies hold the no 1 and no 2 market shares in nand overseas securities firms like nomura have reported that sandisk the no 5 player in the market also plans to raise nand prices by 100 this new year an industry official said similar to dram nand manufacturers are successively joining the price hikes adding in fact price increases across the entire nand market are inevitable the sharp rise in nand prices is due to an imbalance between demand and supply demand continues to grow but supply is insufficient first demand has surged particularly for enterprise solidstate drives essds driven by expanded investments in ai infrastructure additionally the adoption of highperformance highcapacity storage devices in mobiles and pcs has spread this is fueled by the strong trend of ondevice ai where ai computations are performed directly on the end device on the other hand supply has been limited there were no largescale expansions of nand flash production last year and supply volumes did not increase significantly due to process transitions and other factors samsung electronics has also been conservative in nand investments the consensus is that while it did not reach the level of production cuts shipment expansions were restricted nand prices are expected to rise in the second quarter as well samsung electronics is reportedly in discussions with customers for nand supply price increases in q2 the market impact from price hikes in memory such as dram and nand is significant first the cost of building ai infrastructure is rising sharply theres even talk that memory is becoming a bottleneck in ai proliferation price increases for various devices equipped with memory such as smartphones and pcs are also inevitable an industry official stated not only ai data centers but also smartphone and pc manufacturers are planning to raise final product prices due to memory costs adding since memory supply cannot be drastically increased immediately this trend is likely to continue for a while
